blocks.text: Addition of hydrogen to carbon-carbon double bond to form alkane is an example of organic reduction reaction.

Various reducing agents are used in Organic synthesis. e.g; LiAlH₄, NaBH₄, Sn + conc.HCl. Reduction of nitriles to amines, amides to amines, carboxylic acid to primary alcohols, nitrobenzene to phenylamine are all examples of reduction and will be studied in class 12 syllabus.

blocks.prompt: a) Draw the displayed formula and name an isomer of C₄H₈ that could be an example of positional isomerism?
blocks.explanation: But-1-ene, CH₂=CH–CH₂–CH₃, and but-2-ene, CH₃–CH=CH–CH₃, are position isomers of C₄H₈: the same carbon chain with the double bond in a different position.

blocks.prompt: b) What type of isomers are ethoxy methane ether and propanol?
blocks.explanation: Ethoxy methane, CH₃CH₂OCH₃, and propan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂OH, both have the formula C₃H₈O but different functional groups (ether and alcohol), so they are functional group isomers.

blocks.prompt: c) What are the different types of structural isomerism in alkenes?
blocks.explanation: Chain isomerism (but-1-ene and 2-methylpropene), position isomerism (but-1-ene and but-2-ene), and functional group isomerism with cycloalkanes (but-1-ene and cyclobutane).

blocks.prompt: d) Write down different isomers of the compound C₄H₉NH₂.
blocks.explanation: C₄H₉NH₂ (C₄H₁₁N) has four primary amine isomers, in which the –NH₂ group is at a different place on the carbon chain or the chain is branched: butan-1-amine CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂NH₂, butan-2-amine CH₃CH₂CH(NH₂)CH₃, 2-methylpropan-1-amine (CH₃)₂CHCH₂NH₂ and 2-methylpropan-2-amine (CH₃)₃CNH₂. The first two are position isomers; the others are chain isomers. Secondary and tertiary amines of the same formula also exist (for example CH₃CH₂NHCH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH₂N(CH₃)₂), but these four are the ones with an –NH₂ group.
